baseline.definition: Unchanged Phase109 fused checked-source owned graph and ABI; same cached GCC runtime object and exact Phase110 graphs.

objective.primary: Geometric mean of per-workload median worker-seconds candidate / unchanged fused-QBE baseline. Every candidate uses the SAME baseline denominator.
objective.secondary: Select/report best eligible QBE candidate separately as primary no-Clang experiment; report fastest eligible absolute 12-choice candidate separately.
objective.attribution: Also report ratios to unchanged fused of the same worker backend; do not use differing denominators to rank backend winners.
objective.aggregation: Equal weight per predeclared timed training workload. Median of alternating paired rounds; minimum three rounds, target five.
objective.tie: Retain incumbent when improvement <3% or alternating paired results fail to show consistent direction. Use smaller code/build cost only as explanatory tie data, not to overturn uncertainty.
objective.heldout: Freeze training winner first; evaluate heldout once, with no policy/code/data adaptation. Retain incumbent if any heldout correctness failure or heldout geometric-mean worker regression >3%; report any individual >10% regression.

limits.adaptation: No new candidate or post-hoc dataset weighting inside this search. New ideas require a newly timestamped search with explicit reused-heldout status.

qualification: Check all frozen training observations and complete ownership release before performance ranking.
Old Phase109 regressions remain mandatory separate controls.
Heldout results must never train or repair the already selected candidate; preserve failures.
Unsupported candidate profiles stay in search record as unavailable, not omitted.
costAccounting: One-time frontend/runtime acquisition, separately from cache hits.
Worker object build, link, validation, timing and total search wall/CPU.
Worker-only time excludes graph construction, independent observation and release; report those costs separately when available.
Break-even repetitions = incremental build/validation/search cost divided by saved worker seconds for explicitly declared workload; undefined when savings <=0.
Code size and peak bump words; allocator release for every repetition.
Policy search is not recursive acceleration without a frozen-builder/updating-builder equal-budget comparison.
